tools.name: lykoi_admit
tools.description: Persist immutable typed definitions, or record explicit total caller migration. Admission mechanically seals omitted identities, validates with unchanged R6.32/R6.18 contracts, and returns pins. A successor preserves exact name and signature. Migration changes only selected caller dependency pins; null means retain.

tools.name: lykoi_retrieve
tools.description: Read exact admitted immutable definition closure and dependency impact by pin. Returns registry token and successor/migration records; does not rewrite any binding.

tools.name: lykoi_validate
tools.description: Read admitted closed root, expand via unchanged R6.18 and validate frozen VM plan. Returns structured validation identity, node count and provenance map. No execution.

tools.name: lykoi_execute
tools.description: Read, validate and execute admitted closed root on exact input bytes through unchanged R6.10 VM. Returns structured values, errors, spans, trace and logical work.

tools.name: lykoi_library
tools.description: Read only the assigned frozen library or expanded templates. Index or exact relation fetch. No other condition accessible.

tools.name: lykoi_propose
tools.description: Development only. Propose a reusable typed definition implementing one frozen development relation. Semantics and non-applicability must be explicit. Only identities are mechanically sealed; finite development checks precede reusable admission.

tools.name: lykoi_submit
tools.description: Evaluation only. Seal complete Entry artifact by immutable pin. First and final submissions preserved. No acceptance feedback. At most three submissions.

entries.non_applicability: Not applicable when the interval must constrain the fee-adjusted result instead of the original x: with x=10, floor=0, ceiling=10, fee=1, this composition returns 11, while a requirement to keep x+fee within [0,10] would reject it.
entries.semantics: For Int64 parameters in the exact order x, floor, ceiling, fee: first check floor <= x, failing with RANGE_LOW at site x if false; next check x <= ceiling, failing with RANGE_HIGH at site x if false; only after both checks pass, evaluate the checked Int64 addition x + fee and return it. Both checks refer to the original x, not the fee-adjusted result. If both range conditions are false, RANGE_LOW takes precedence. Addition uses the existing add expression and its existing checked arithmetic semantics.

entries.non_applicability: Not applicable when only the combined sum must lie between 2*floor and cap, without requiring each input to meet floor: for x=-1, y=5, floor=0, cap=10, the sum 4 meets that combined bound, but this composition fails with FIRST_LOW at site -1.
entries.semantics: For Int64 parameters in the exact order x, y, floor, cap: first check floor <= x, failing with FIRST_LOW at site x if false; then check floor <= y, failing with SECOND_LOW at site y if false. After both checks pass, evaluate x + y using the existing checked Int64 add semantics. Check that this sum <= cap, failing with TOTAL_HIGH at site y if false. Return the sum only after that check passes. The stated check order determines failure precedence; the cap constrains the combined sum, not either input individually.

arguments.semantics: For Int64 parameters in exact order x, y, expected, limit, bias: first check x == expected, failing with KEY_MISMATCH at site x if false; then check y <= limit, failing with LOAD_HIGH at site y if false. Only after both checks pass, compute and return ((x + y) + y) + bias, with each addition using existing checked Int64 add semantics in that exact left-associated order. KEY_MISMATCH takes precedence when both checks would fail. The limit constrains the original y, not the doubled load or final result; bias is applied only in the final addition.
arguments.non_applicability: Not applicable when limit constrains the doubled load rather than the original y: x=3, y=4, expected=3, limit=5, bias=1 passes this composition and returns 12, whereas a requirement that y+y <= limit would reject it.
